_meta.what: Dated record of the MRR (Meridian Research Runtime) line — the engineering track, not the Meridian collective's research voice (enc-2026-005, authorship honesty).
_meta.rule: Every entry names a commit and says only what that commit records. No entry is written ahead of the work it reports; nothing here is summarised from intent.
_meta.why: /on-record renders one export snapshot and stays fixed at its date by design (the derivation is deterministic — no network, no clock, no model). This log is what carries the runtime's later state onto the site, per the currency rule of 2026-07-25.

entries.headline: The runtime called a real model for the first time — and the first answer was wrong.
entries.note: A pinned model (gemini-2.5-flash-lite, pinned rather than a sliding alias) answered in 122 tokens, end state completed. Asked for the most-cited failure mode of model collapse, it named "mode collapse" — checked against the repository's pinned theory atlas (87 entries) that term appears zero times, and the canonical definition describes something else entirely: distribution tails vanishing over recursive generations. Two different concepts, similar symptom, separate literature. The first real call produced, in 87 words, exactly what the system is built against: a fluent, self-assured answer that is wrong at a checkable point. The adapter logged it as completed and was right to — a content error is not visible at the wire; refusal detects silence, not error.

entries.headline: Redirects are refused, not followed.
entries.note: Source and citation fetching no longer follows HTTP redirects. A redirect can move a pinned source somewhere else between the pinning and the reading; following it silently would mean the evidence on record is not the evidence that was fetched. The fetch now refuses instead.

entries.headline: The export that On Record renders.
entries.note: One claim-rooted RO-Crate + W3C-PROV export, committed to this repository as the archive. Every figure on /on-record is a SPARQL query over it — which is also why that page does not move on its own: it shows this snapshot, dated, and nothing later.
